question: A can contains 40 litres of oil at Rs. 50/litre. Another can contains 60 litres of oil at Rs. 60/litre. They are mixed, and 20 litres are sold at Rs. 70/litre. How much profit or loss does the seller make on this sale?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average CP per litre = (40 × 50 + 60 × 60) ÷ 100 = Rs. 56

Selling Price (SP) per litre = Rs. 70

Profit per litre = SP − CP = 70 − 56 = Rs. 14

Total profit on 20 litres sold = 20 × 14 = Rs. 280

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 280 profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quantity of Can 1 = 40 litres at Rs. 50/litre

Quantity of Can 2 = 60 litres at Rs. 60/litre

Quantity sold = 20 litres at Rs. 70/litre

**Formula Used:**

Average CP = Total Cost ÷ Total Quantity

Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP)
